findings.text: `Servex/Heartbeat.js:150`, `Servex/Lifecycle.js:121,171,347` and `Servex/Worktrees.js:226` call `SessionRecord` but never import it (checked on branch `worktree/session-record`), so each throws a ReferenceError at runtime; `node --check` cannot catch this. Heartbeat and Lifecycle's `recent_tasks` crash outright, and the calls inside `try {} catch {}` fail silently: Lifecycle stops writing the worktree line, and Worktrees skips every task, so the worktree-owner map comes back empty. Add `import SessionRecord from "../Server/SessionRecord.mjs";` to all three.

`Server/DaySpend.mjs:177` calls `SessionRecord.log_file(dateDir, d.name)`, and `Server/task-cost.mjs:128` calls `log_file(AI, date, d.name)`, but `log_file(dir)` takes one argument. Both check the day folder itself, fall back to `task.jsonl`, and so leave every moved session folder out of the day spend and out of `task-cost --date`. Pass `join(dateDir, d.name)` (and `join(AI, date, d.name)`).

Requirement 4 is not done yet. The plan is 699 folders, under the 800 cap, so `--apply` should run, but `ai/sessions/session-record-moves.jsonl` does not exist, and the task log ends at "readers patched" with no apply, headless render check, undo-on-a-copy or landing line. Fix 1 and 2 before the apply, or the live Servex mis-reads the moved folders.

Requirement 1's "588 collide" premise was checked and found false (0 folders hold both files; the 588 are digest-only), and `doc/session-record.md` says so clearly. The extra `fold` action, the `--quiet` skip for active logs, and `append.mjs` following a moved record are all sensible additions with tests.

Simpler: the same expression `SessionRecord.log_file(x) ?? path.join(x, "task.jsonl")` is pasted into about 30 call sites, and that copy-paste is how bug 2 got in. A static `SessionRecord.log_or_old(dir)` would make each call site one short, uniform call. `SessionIndex.seal` (`Server/SessionIndex.mjs:74`) also calls `log_file` twice on one line.

`is_log_entry` opens and reads 2 KB of every `task.jsonl`/`session.jsonl` it walks past (`SessionRecord.mjs:319-329`), across about 1,600 folders, on every walk (TaskLoop, SessionIndex, ledger). Cheap enough today, but it is a filename check that became a file read.

`core/Item/Store.js:576-595` now makes a HEAD request before every `task.jsonl` store opens, on production too. On a static host a missing file may come back as a 200 HTML page; the `content-type` check covers that case, so this is fine, but it adds a round trip to every task page.

Writers (`TaskDirs --new`, the first line `spawn_agent` writes) still create `task.jsonl` for new session folders, so the rule only holds after a re-run. The doc says so under "What is not done yet", and it should get a follow-up task, not just a line in the doc.

The fence allowed "one small change each" in the readers listed in step 1; the diff touches 37 files, including `Servex/` (so `needs_restart` applies) and `core/Item/Store.js`. The edits are each small, and the wide reach is justified by the grep, but it goes past the brief's list.

findings.text: Some readers of a session folder's log are still unpatched: `Server/on-landing.mjs:25`, `Server/review.mjs:98` (`readTaskJsonl`), `Server/LandingCheck.mjs:22` and `Server/plugins/CardAnswer.js:202` all still hard-code `path.join(dir, "task.jsonl")`. After `--apply` moves 699 folders, these readers will see an empty log for a moved session folder, and `on-landing` would append to a new `task.jsonl` beside the moved record (a later run then has to fold it back in). Patch them the same one-line way, or list them in the doc as "not yet" with the reason.

`sessions/doc/session-record.md` ("Readers: every one accepts both names") says every reader is covered. A grep on branch `worktree/session-record` finds about 30 files under `Server/` that still name `task.jsonl` with no `SessionRecord`. Most of them are fine, because they read task folders or are tests. The brief asked for the list of readers, so the doc should name the ones it checked and left alone (TaskHomes, HandoverNow and `session-*` were named in the brief and don't appear in the doc).

The round-1 fixes are in (`05588bdfd`): `Heartbeat.js`, `Lifecycle.js` and `Worktrees.js` now import `SessionRecord`, and `DaySpend.mjs` and `task-cost.mjs` pass the folder path. `node Server/SessionRecord.test.mjs` prints "ok", and `node --check` passes on every changed `.js`/`.mjs`.

`public/framework/ai/AISession/StoreFolder.js:105` now routes any folder holding a `session.jsonl` to an `AITask` page. That includes the 588 folders with digest tags only, which used to show as a plain folder. `Store.record_url` (`core/Item/Store.js`) will then load the tag-only file as if it were a task log. The node side guards against this with `log_file()` returning null, so the doc's claim "never shows up as a phantom task" is true only on the node side. Check one of the 588 in the headless render pass.

Requirement 4's apply, manifest, headless render of three session pages and undo-on-a-copy are still to come. `ai/sessions/session-record-moves.jsonl` does not exist yet. That order is correct (the brief puts the data move after the merge), but the task can't land until those lines are in its log.

Simpler: `SessionRecord.log_file(x) ?? path.join(x, "task.jsonl")` is still pasted into about 30 call sites. `SessionIndex.seal` (`Server/SessionIndex.mjs:74`) still calls `log_file` twice on one line. A static `SessionRecord.log_or_old(dir)` would make finding 1's patches one short, uniform call each.

After the move, `AISession.record()` (used by `Server/session-summary.mjs:130`) reads a `session.jsonl` that also holds the whole task log. It looks like it picks only its own verbs. Spot-check one session-summary run after the apply, to confirm the tags, alerts and links come out unchanged.

The item tool will treat a moved session folder as a `Session`, not a `Task`. `Servex/agents/page_tools.js:349` maps `session.jsonl` to the `Session` class (core/Session/Session.js, with `SESSION_KEYS`). After `--apply`, `item({path: <session folder>})` replays the log with the wrong class, and Task verbs (`start`, `wait`, `finish`, `log`) can be refused. Before the apply, either map a session folder's `session.jsonl` whose line 1 is an `assign` to `Task` (`SessionRecord.log_file` already tells them apart), or list this as a blocker in the doc.

`Servex/agents/Global.js:514` still builds the caller's log as `path.join(dir, "task.jsonl")`. `page_tools.js:622` echoes every item call into that path with `write_line`, which skips `append.mjs`. So after the move, each item call by a session agent recreates `task.jsonl` beside `session.jsonl`. Every reader prefers `session.jsonl` (`SessionRecord.log_file`), so it misses those lines until a later `--apply` runs a "fold". Use `SessionRecord.log_or_old(dir)` there. The same file's `page_tools.js:458/465/553` (child task logs) correctly keep `task.jsonl`.

The doc's "Readers" list (`sessions/doc/session-record.md`) is still incomplete. On branch `worktree/session-record`, these files name `task.jsonl` without `SessionRecord`, and the doc names none of them, patched or "left alone": `Servex/agents/Global.js`, `Dispatcher.js`, `Brief.js`, `Echo.js`, `Servex/Pool.js`, `Budget.js`, `Servex.js`, `asks/Asks.js`, `asks/stalled.js`, `Server/plugins/AILogs.js`, `Assistant.js`, `health-supervisor.mjs`, `git-hooks/post-commit.mjs`, `jsonl-keep.mjs`, `smoke.mjs`, `CardCheck.mjs`, `ArchiveCopy.mjs`, `ArchiveSessions.mjs`. Many of them only mention the name in a comment or a prompt, and `post-commit.mjs` goes through `append.mjs`, which follows the move. But the brief asked for the list, and `HandoverNow` (named in the brief) is still not mentioned.

The rule "told apart by their verb" is not quite true. `note` is both a task.jsonl verb (`jsonl-schema.mjs`) and a digest verb (`SessionRecord.TAG_VERBS`), and folders such as `sessions/2026/10/02/node-reap/task.jsonl` hold `{"note":…}` lines. After the rename, `AISession.record()` (`ai/AISession/AISession.js:494`) will count those log notes as record notes. Say so in the doc, or have `record()` skip lines in the log's own shape.

`ai/AISession/StoreFolder.js:105` still sends the 588 tag-only folders to an `AITask` page, and `Store.record_url` then loads the tag file as a task log. The node side guards against this (`log_file` returns null). The browser side does not, so the doc's "never shows up as a phantom task" is only half true. This was raised in round 2 and is still open; check one tag-only folder in the headless render pass.

`ai/AISession/AISessionIndex.mjs:176` hard-codes `task.jsonl` for the category join. It reads from `ai/2026-10-08/task-audit`, a path that is probably already stale after the earlier archive move, so this is low risk. One line in the doc would cover it.

`Server/SessionRecord.mjs` itself looks right. The merge and fold do append + rename with line-count and byte checks, undo splits by the recorded counts and refuses to overwrite, and the test covers rename, merge, fold, skip, a missing final newline, undo and `append.mjs` following the move. Small thing: `SessionIndex.seal` (`Server/SessionIndex.mjs:74`) calls `log_file` twice per record; a local variable is simpler.

Requirement 4 is not done yet: the apply, `session-record-moves.jsonl` (absent), the headless render of the Sessions page plus three session pages, and the undo on a copy. The order is correct (code merged first), but the task must not land until those lines are in `task.jsonl`.

The round-3 fixes are in (`0aac4c7c7`). `Servex/agents/page_tools.js:380` (`class_of`) now replays a moved session log as a `Task`, `Servex/agents/Global.js:515` uses `SessionRecord.log_or_old(dir)`, and `sessions/doc/session-record.md` lists every reader it patched and every one it left alone, with the reason (TaskHomes is included). `node Server/SessionRecord.test.mjs` prints "ok", `node --check` passes on every changed `.js`/`.mjs`, and `--plan` on the main tree still gives rename 699 · merge 0 · fold 0 · skip 58 · already 588, which matches the doc.

The code is not merged yet: `worktree/session-record` is not in `michael/dev`. Requirement 4's remaining steps also have no trace yet: the `--apply` commit, `ai/sessions/session-record-moves.jsonl` (absent), the headless render of the Sessions page plus three session pages (one should be a tag-only folder, which tests `StoreFolder.js:105`), and `--undo` on a copy. The order is right, but the task must not land until those lines are in `task.jsonl`.

New session folders will keep getting a `task.jsonl`, because `TaskDirs.mjs --new` and the first `assign` write in `Agents.js` still create it. `append.mjs:44` follows the move only when `task.jsonl` is missing. Until the writers switch, `--apply` has to be re-run now and then, and the doc says so. Make it a real follow-up (a card or a child brief), not just a line in the doc.

`ext/JSONL/JSONL.js:51` sets `this.url` only after the `record_url` HEAD request resolves. If `unsubscribe()` runs before that, `drop(this)` misses, and the stream subscribes afterwards and leaks. This is rare and low impact. Every `task.jsonl` open (in `Store.open` and in `live`) now also costs an extra HEAD request.

Requirement 2 asked to name and run the scripts that rebuild `index.json` and `directory.json`. The doc's last bullet says neither needs a rebuild, because `index.json` mentions `task.jsonl` only inside titles. That is a reasonable call, but confirm it by grepping `directory.json` after the apply.

It could be simpler. About 30 call sites still spell out `SessionRecord.log_file(x) ?? path.join(x, "task.jsonl")` instead of calling the `log_or_old(x)` helper that now exists (for example `Agents.js:28,775,835,847,1347,1858,1880` and `tools.js:99,112`). They behave the same, so a later sweep is enough.
